problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14060128/assets/93c6184f39b28a057866bb02e11e5e81a7abea4ff8a9a907670dd30cfc93d557.png)

The path ${C}_{1}$ consists of a line segment from the point $A(1,-1)$ to the point $B(1,1),$ and the path ${C}_{2}$ consists of a line segment from the point $B(1,1)$ to the point $O(0,0).$

Given that ${\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r=2,$ evaluate ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=(2x+y)\,i+(x-2y)\,j,$ and $C={C}_{1}\cup {C}_{2}.$
worked_solution:
We will use the fact that

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r.
$$

We're given the value of the first integral, so we only need to work out the second.

The path ${C}_{2}$ is the line segment from $B$ to $O.$ It can be parametrized as

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{2}(t) & =b+t(0-b) \\  & =⟨1,1⟩+t(⟨0,0⟩-⟨1,1⟩) \\  & =⟨1-t,1-t⟩ \\  & =(1-t)\,i+(1-t)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $0<t<1.$ Along this segment, we have $x=1-t$ and $y=1-t.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F({r}_{2}(t)) & =(2x+y)\,i+(x-2y)\,j \\  & =(2(1-t)+(1-t))\,i+((1-t)-2(1-t))\,j \\  & =(3-3t)\,i+(-1+t)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the derivative, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{2}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-t)j \\  & =-i-j\end{aligned}
$$

We can now compute the dot product:

$$
\begin{aligned}F({r}_{2}(t))\cdot {r}_{2}^{′}(t) & =((3-3t)\,i+(-1+t)\,j)\cdot (-i-j) \\  & =-3+3t+1-t \\  & =-2+2t\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can evaluate the integral, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r \\  & =2+{\int }_{0}^{1}F({r}_{2}(t))\cdot {r}_{2}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =2+{\int }_{0}^{1}(-2+2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =2+(-2t+{t}^{2})\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =2+(1-2) \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Given that ∫C1F⋅dr=2, evaluate ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=(2x+y)i+(x−2y)j, and C=C1∪C2.

EXPLANATION

We will use the fact that ∫CF⋅dr=∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr.

We're given the value of the first integral, so we only need to work out the second.

The path C2 is the line segment from B to O. It can be parametrized as r2(t)=b+t(0−b)=⟨1,1⟩+t(⟨0,0⟩−⟨1,1⟩)=⟨1−t,1−t⟩=(1−t)i+(1−t)j, where 0<t<1. Along this segment, we have x=1−t and y=1−t. Therefore, F(r2(t))=(2x+y)i+(x−2y)j=(2(1−t)+(1−t))i+((1−t)−2(1−t))j=(3−3t)i+(−1+t)j.

Computing the derivative, we get the following: r2′(t)=ddt(1−t)i+ddt(1−t)j=−i−j

We can now compute the dot product: F(r2(t))⋅r2′(t)=((3−3t)i+(−1+t)j)⋅(−i−j)=−3+3t+1−t=−2+2t

Finally, we can evaluate the integral, as follows: ∫CF⋅dr=∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr=2+∫01F(r2(t))⋅r2′(t)dt=2+∫01(−2+2t)dt=2+(−2t+t2)|01=2+(1−2)=1
